title: Pride and Prejudice
synopsis: Longbourn, regency England. A single man in possession of a good fortune is in want of a wife. Your mother is, somehow, aware of every such man in the county.

nodes.text: Bingley has taken Netherfield. Mama is, immediately, planning.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Indulge her.” The story records the instinct as “Civil” and carries it forward.
There is no taking “Tease her” back. Spirit shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Bingley is amiable. His friend Darcy is, instantly, insufferable.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Wit—follows you into whatever comes next.
There is no taking “Be wounded” back. Honest shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Darcy says you are tolerable but not handsome enough to tempt him. Charlotte overhears.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Laugh it off” back. Pride shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You commit to “File it away.” The story records the instinct as “Honest” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Jane is sent to Netherfield in the rain. She catches cold.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Walk to nurse her.” The story records the instinct as “Sister” and carries it forward.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Modesty.

nodes.text: You arrive at Netherfield, muddy. The Bingley sisters notice.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Ignore them” back. Spirit shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Civil.

nodes.text: He watches you across rooms. You assume the worst of him.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Spirit—follows you into whatever comes next.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Honest.

nodes.text: A cousin, awful, proposes. He will inherit Longbourn.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Refuse” back. Self shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Family.

nodes.text: Your friend marries him. You are, at first, hurt.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Honor.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Pride—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: A charming officer. He tells you Darcy ruined him.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Believe him.” The story records the instinct as “Sympathetic” and carries it forward.
There is no taking “Doubt him” back. Wise shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: You visit Charlotte. Lady Catherine de Bourgh is, somehow, much.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Civil.
You commit to “Spar.” The story records the instinct as “Spirit” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: He proposes, against his will. He is, in proposing, awful.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honor—follows you into whatever comes next.
There is no taking “Hesitate” back. Honest shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: He writes you a letter. Wickham is, in fact, a scoundrel.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Reread it” back. Wise shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Pride.

nodes.text: You tour, by chance. The house is, mortifyingly, lovely.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Admire it.” The story records the instinct as “Honest” and carries it forward.
“Mock it” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Pride.

nodes.text: He returns early. He is, against expectation, kind.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Civil.
There is no taking “Be flustered” back. Honest shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Your youngest sister has run off with Wickham.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Family.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Civil—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: He, secretly, arranges the marriage and pays Wickham's debts.

choices.consequence: “Suspect him gratefully” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honor.
“Suspect uncle” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Naive.

nodes.text: She demands you promise not to marry her nephew.

choices.consequence: “Refuse to promise” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Spirit.
You commit to “Pretend.” The story records the instinct as “Strategy” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Darcy proposes again. Differently.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Heart.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Honor.

nodes.text: Mama, hearing, almost faints with joy.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Family.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Patient—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: A double wedding for Jane and you. Darcy stands tall. Bingley smiles.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Path—follows you into whatever comes next.
There is no taking “Take Jane's hand first” back. Sister shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: You walk the library with the master of it. The shelves are higher than the house in Hertfordshire.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Read often” back. Joy shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You commit to “Manage the estate.” The story records the instinct as “Duty” and carries it forward.
Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: You manage Pemberley with grace. The Darcy heirs are, mercifully, more like their father than your mother. Lady Catherine, eventually, visits.
Jane and you live within a day's ride. Your children grow up together. You are, in middle age, sometimes silly with her in the way of girls in a sitting room.
You write, late in life, a quiet anonymous novel about a country family with too many daughters. It does, surprisingly, well.
